newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler to spend $400 million on move.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to spend $400 million on move.

text.p: The United Auto Workers' tentative pact with Chrysler Corp., which mirrors the terms of the union's agreement with Ford Motor Co., also commits Chrysler to spend $400 million to relocate its Jeep and Truck Engineering group.

The move, which will occur in 1999, will add 550 existing salaried Chrysler workers to the UAW's membership rolls at the company. The union represents about 60,000 hourly and 6,000 salaried workers at the automaker.

Details of the agreement were provided to reporters on Thursday at a meeting of the UAW-Chrysler National Council. The council, made up of plant-level officers, was expected to approve the tentative deal. UAW officials were not available to provide final results.
All of Chrysler's UAW locals are scheduled to hold ratification votes by Oct. 13. Chrysler and the UAW reached their agreement Sept. 29.

Jeep and Truck Engineering (JTE), now located in Detroit, will be moved to a new facility to be built at the Chrysler Technology Centre in Auburn Hills, Mich. The unit is the former engineering centre for American Motors Corp., which Chrysler bought in 1987.

About 3,200 people, working in advanced manufacturing, engineering design and administrative support, are now at JTE, which handles most of the design and testing for Chrysler's Jeep and light truck products.
Chrysler spokeswoman Nicole Solomon said the company had previously planned to move those operations to its headquarters complex.
"We've always said we wanted our vehicle-making functions and our headquarters to be in the same place," she said.

It is too early to tell if all of the JTE workers will be relocated to Auburn Hills, although most of them are expected to make the move, Solomon said. Construction on a new building is not expected to begin until 1998. The company has not decided what will be done with the four-story building.
Economic terms of the labour contract, as expected, provide job security guarantees and economic gains of more than $13,900 for hourly UAW members at Chrysler.
For hourly workers, Chrysler agreed to make lump sump payments of $2,000 in the first year, followed by 3 percent base wage gains in the second and third years.

UAW salaried workers at Chrysler will receive gains of up to $15,400 under the tentative pact. That includes a lump sum payment of $2,000 in the first year, salary increases of 3 percent to 4 percent in the second year, and a 3 percent increase in the third year.
Chrysler has about 6,000 salaried workers represented by the UAW, the most of any of the U.S. Big Three automakers.
